summary: Envoy Sidecar Proxy Memory Leak in Trade Execution Service
problem_description:
impactedApplication: Equities Trade Execution Service
rootCause: An Envoy proxy version (1.28.0) had a memory leak in the HTTP/2 codec when handling large response headers from the market data feed. Memory grew by 50MB/hour per pod until the OOM killer terminated sidecars.
mitigation: Upgraded Envoy to 1.28.2 which patched the HTTP/2 codec leak, reduced market data response header size by compressing metadata, and added container memory usage alerts at 80% of limit.
accountableParty: Platform Engineering
sourceSystem: Istio / Envoy Proxy
repeatIncident: False
executiveSummary: Trade execution latency degraded progressively over 8 hours as Envoy sidecar proxies leaked memory. Starting at 06:00 UTC, pods began being OOMKilled at random intervals, causing 340 trade execution timeouts across equities desks.
steps_taken: Detection & Triage: Sporadic pod restarts were observed starting at 06:00 UTC. By 10:00 UTC, the restart frequency increased to every 15 minutes. Container memory metrics showed a linear growth pattern in Envoy sidecars. Engineers identified Envoy 1.28.0 as the culprit after correlating with the upstream CVE advisory. Emergency upgrade to 1.28.2 was deployed via canary rollout. All memory leak symptoms stopped after the upgrade. Impacted trades were reconciled through the end-of-day matching process.
root_cause_analysis: Envoy 1.28.0 HTTP/2 codec memory leak with large response headers

summary: Deadlock in Distributed Transaction Coordinator During Month-End Batch
problem_description:
impactedApplication: Month-End Financial Close Batch System
rootCause: Two competing batch jobs acquired locks on the same pair of database tables in reverse order, creating a classic AB-BA deadlock. The transaction coordinator's deadlock detection timeout was set to 10 minutes, leaving both jobs stuck.
mitigation: Restarted the transaction coordinator with forced lock release, reordered batch job lock acquisition to follow a consistent global ordering, and reduced deadlock detection timeout from 10 minutes to 30 seconds.
accountableParty: Batch Processing Team
sourceSystem: Oracle Database / Spring Batch
repeatIncident: True
executiveSummary: The month-end financial close batch system stalled for 2.5 hours starting at 01:00 UTC. The GL aggregation and intercompany elimination jobs deadlocked each other, blocking all downstream reporting jobs and delaying the financial close deadline.
steps_taken: Detection & Triage: Batch job monitoring showed two jobs stuck in RUNNING state with no progress at 01:15 UTC. Database administrators confirmed an AB-BA deadlock between the GL_ENTRIES and IC_ELIMINATION tables. The deadlock detection mechanism had a 10-minute timeout, and both jobs had been configured with infinite retry on lock acquisition. Engineers force-killed the deadlocked sessions and restarted the batch with corrected job ordering. The financial close completed 2.5 hours behind schedule. Post-incident, all batch jobs were audited for lock ordering consistency and the detection timeout was reduced.
root_cause_analysis: AB-BA deadlock between competing batch jobs

summary: Kafka Schema Registry Incompatible Evolution Breaks Consumers
problem_description:
impactedApplication: Real-Time Risk Calculation Pipeline
rootCause: A producer deployed an Avro schema change that removed a required field (counterparty_id) without following backward-compatible evolution rules. The Schema Registry accepted it because compatibility was set to NONE instead of BACKWARD.
mitigation: Reverted the schema to the previous version, restored BACKWARD compatibility enforcement on all production subjects, and added a CI gate that validates schema compatibility before allowing merges.
accountableParty: Data Platform Team
sourceSystem: Confluent Schema Registry / Kafka
repeatIncident: False
executiveSummary: All downstream consumers of the risk-events topic crashed with deserialization errors at 09:30 UTC after a producer deployed an incompatible Avro schema change. The real-time risk calculation pipeline was down for 55 minutes, leaving the trading desk without live risk metrics.
steps_taken: Detection & Triage: Consumer crash alerts fired at 09:30 UTC with SerializationException errors. Investigation traced the failure to a schema change deployed at 09:25 UTC that removed the counterparty_id field. The Schema Registry had compatibility set to NONE for the risk-events subject, allowing the breaking change through. Engineers reverted the schema registration and restarted all consumers. The pipeline recovered by 10:25 UTC. Post-incident, all Schema Registry subjects were audited and set to BACKWARD compatibility. A pre-merge CI check was added that tests schema evolution against the registry.
root_cause_analysis: Incompatible Avro schema change with NONE compatibility setting
